To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
coherent streamwise vortical structures near the wall of turbulent channel flow are elongated and tilted and are responsible for the observed near wall phenomena.
the near-wall CS array is a staggered array of highly elongated vortices tilted in the streamwise x direction.
the dominant CS near the wall are quasi streamwise vorticities that are highly elongated, staggered in space, and tilted in both the x, y and x, z planes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new vortex definition, its application to a turbulent channel flow and the elucidation of the physical mechanisms responsible for near wall CS dynamics.
the development and validation of a coherent structure model which is consistent with the near wall data, as well as with the global properties of a turbulent channel flow.
the development and testing of a new vortex definition for the detection and analysis of CS in wall-bounded turbulent flows.

the near wall CS are quasi streamwise v or tices, tilted in the x, z direction, which are responsible for the majority of near wall events.
the near wall CS array is a dominant feature of the flow, and is responsible for sustaining itself, and the entire turbulent flow field.

coherent structures in the near wall region are quasi-streamwise vortices which are tilted in the x, y plane.
